get.description: Private/no-store masked CSRF bootstrap. Works with CSRF_COOKIE_HTTPONLY and CSRF_USE_SESSIONS. May establish framework CSRF/session state; never creates accounts or player data. No query parameters.

post.description: CSRF-protected JSON login, including anonymous requests. Uses Django authentication backends and session fixation protection. Invalid/unknown/inactive credentials share a generic invalid_credentials 400 response. Success returns minimal identity and a rotated CSRF token. No redirects, next field or query parameters.

post.description: CSRF-protected logout, including anonymous callers. Accepts an empty body or empty JSON object only. Flushes the current auth session, rotates CSRF and returns anonymous identity plus a fresh token. No redirects or query parameters; repeated valid-CSRF logout remains anonymous.

parameters.description: Token returned by the CSRF bootstrap or last successful login/logout; send the corresponding same-origin cookies.
parameters.name: X-CSRFToken

post.description: CSRF-protected recovery request with required email. Same acknowledgement for eligible, unknown, inactive or unusable-password accounts and mail delivery failure. Links use only configured public origin, never request Host/forwarded headers. Current Django email-match eligibility is preserved. Delivery is synchronous; no constant-time guarantee. Missing/unsafe destination configuration returns 503 for every valid email.

parameters.description: Token returned by the CSRF bootstrap or last successful login/logout; send the corresponding same-origin cookies.
parameters.name: X-CSRFToken

post.description: CSRF-protected password reset using uidb64/token and new_password1/new_password2 JSON. Token revalidation and SetPasswordForm save are atomic under a user-row lock, shared with HTML confirmation. Success requires a separate login; existing target sessions become invalid by Django's password hash. No user details/token are returned. Invalid links share invalid_reset_token 400; password errors are field-specific.

parameters.description: Token returned by the CSRF bootstrap or last successful login/logout; send the corresponding same-origin cookies.
parameters.name: X-CSRFToken

post.description: CSRF-protected reset link check with uidb64/token in JSON, not URL/query. Valid links return valid=true without consuming the token or disclosing account data. Invalid, unknown-user, inactive, expired or used links share invalid_reset_token 400. Confirmation rechecks under a row lock.

parameters.description: Token returned by the CSRF bootstrap or last successful login/logout; send the corresponding same-origin cookies.
parameters.name: X-CSRFToken

post.description: CSRF-protected JSON registration using the existing UserRegisterForm, password validators and profile signals. Requires username, email, password1 and password2. User/profile writes are atomic; both web flows serialize case-insensitive username collisions. Success requires a separate login and preserves the caller's session. Email remains required but non-unique, matching existing policy. No redirects or query parameters.

parameters.description: Token returned by the CSRF bootstrap or last successful login/logout; send the corresponding same-origin cookies.
parameters.name: X-CSRFToken

get.description: Private/no-store session discovery for anonymous or authenticated callers. Anonymous/expired/inactive sessions return authenticated=false and user=null, without redirects. Only the current user's ID and username are exposed. No query parameters.

Requires JSON object, session and CSRF; rejects unknown fields/queries, files and privilege/password inputs. Uses shared HTML forms, normalized case-insensitive username policy and the registration name lock. Omitted fields are preserved; empty object is a no-op. User/profile writes and response serialization are atomic under owner/profile locks. Missing profile returns 409 account_profile_unavailable. No password/session rotation or image writes.

parameters.description: Token returned by the CSRF bootstrap or last successful login/logout; send the corresponding same-origin cookies.
